title: Cavity-only optimization with fixed 6-pair Bragg mirrors
scientific_hypothesis: Fixing the outer Bragg mirror stacks to deterministic quarter-wave thicknesses at 550 nm and optimizing only the 4 central cavity layers initialized at half-wave optical thickness for 1547.5 nm will eliminate multi-order phase ambiguity, improve numerical convergence, and achieve target scores >0.95 by refining the passband center wavelength and FWHM without destabilizing the visible stopband.
design_principle: Decoupled optimization: stable photonic stopband from fixed quarter-wave Bragg mirrors, tunable transmission resonance from cavity layer thicknesses. Reduces optimization dimensionality from 30 to 4 variables.
proposed_topology: Air | (HfO2/SiO2)_6 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | (HfO2/SiO2)_6 | Fused Silica substrate. Total 28 finite layers: layers 0-11 (input Bragg, 12 layers), layers 12-15 (cavity, 4 layers), layers 16-27 (output Bragg, 12 layers).
manufacturing_considerations: quarter-wave mirror layers at 550 nm are standard deposition targets
cavity layers near 350-550 nm thickness range are fabricable with standard monitoring
theory_basis: Transfer-matrix method for coherent planar multilayers
Distributed Bragg reflector theory for quarter-wave stacks
Defect-cavity resonance condition: optical thickness = m*λ/2
expected_advantages: Fixed mirrors preserve visible stopband performance from iteration_07
Cavity-only tuning refines telecom passband without destabilizing mirrors
known_risks: Fixed mirror thicknesses may not be globally optimal for dual-band objective
Cavity resonance may split into multiple orders if optical thickness exceeds λ
Numerical convergence may still fail if cavity initialization is far from optimum
execution_request_english: Design a 28-layer defect-cavity dichroic coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence using alternating HfO2 and SiO2. Stack topology: layers 0-11 are fixed quarter-wave Bragg mirror (HfO2/SiO2 repeated 6 times, HfO2 first, optical thickness λ0/4 at 550 nm), layers 12-15 are cavity (HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, initialized at half-wave optical thickness λc/2 at 1547.5 nm using nominal refractive indices), layers 16-27 are fixed quarter-wave Bragg mirror (HfO2/SiO2 repeated 6 times, HfO2 first, optical thickness λ0/4 at 550 nm). Optimize only the 4 cavity layer thicknesses (layers 12-15) with bounds 200-600 nm. Keep all 24 mirror layer thicknesses fixed at their quarter-wave values. Evaluate spectrum from 400-1600 nm at normal incidence, unpolarized. Objective: maximize transmission in 1530-1565 nm, maximize reflection in 400-700 nm. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with 100 iterations maximum. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 400-700 nm, 1530-1565 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1530–1565 nm; high reflection in 400–700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: reflection in 1530–1565 nm; transmission in 400–700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 30.
revision_reason: Direct implementation of feedback directive: fix outer Bragg stacks to deterministic 6-pair topology, initialize cavity to λ/(2n_eff) at 1547.5 nm, optimize only 4 cavity variables to address numerical_convergence failure category from iterations 03 and 07.
